messages:
Sam: Quick update — finished initial quant runs for CeruleanX-10b (int6). TL;DR: ~2.8x token cost reduction vs fp16, but we see a ~4.5% drop in longform recall on our QA slice. p95 latency is a bit worse on cache misses. Posting quick numbers and a proposed mitigation.
Nina: can you paste the numbers so I can brief product?
Sam: sure. Key deltas (fp16 -> int6): ExactMatch 81.2 -> 76.7, Rouge-L 85.0 -> 82.1, avg throughput 350 tps -> 820 tps, unit token cost $0.012 -> $0.0043. Observed longform failure modes: hallucination rate up small amount on retrieval prompts, and multi-turn consistency drops.
Arjun: instruction-following ok for short prompts?
Sam: yes for short single-turn tasks it's comparable. Most regression shows up when: (a) prompt has >1024 tokens, or (b) retrieval hits present and model needs to synthesize many facts.
maria: for summarizer product that could be problematic. 4-5% EM drop is borderline. Do we have a routing/redirection play?
Sam: proposing hybrid routing: int6 default, but route to fp16 for requests with either product tag "summarizer" OR seq_len > 1024 OR has_retrieval=true. Simulation: with a 70/30 split (70% int6 short tasks, 30% fp16 long/retrieval), expected cost ~56% lower than all-fp16 while keeping quality ~98% of fp16 on the overall workload.
cheng: what's the latency picture? p50/p95 numbers?
Sam: measured under canary load: fp16 p50=45ms p95=210ms; int6 p50=38ms p95=240ms. So median faster on int6 but tail slightly worse due to larger KV footprint and cold misses.
Arjun: KV cache warm behavior OK? Any extra memory pressure?
cheng: int6 warms slower on first few tokens but stabilizes. Memory pressure on the host + cache is +8% vs fp16. No OOMs in tests.
Nina: ops concerns? fallback complexity?
Sam: minimal. We can implement policy in routing layer: tag-based override -> length heuristic -> default fleet. Fallback logic: if quality.delta for a slice > 0.02 (2% EM drop) for 30m window, auto-failover that slice to fp16.
ops-bot: Deploy plan queued: canary/ceruleanx-int6-v1 -> 5% traffic / 48h. Link: https://deploy.internal/ceruleanx/1234
maria: product asks for thresholds and canary signals to watch.
Sam: propose signals: EM_delta, RougeL_delta, hallucination_rate, p95_latency, kv_hit_ratio, and unit_cost. Alerts: EM_delta >= 0.02 (absolute) or p95 latency degrade >20% -> trigger rollback.
Arjun: can you drop the unit economics calc for GTN deck?
Sam: quick calc snippet: assume 1M requests/mo, avg tokens/request=200. fp16 cost: $0.012/token -> monthly = 1_000_000 * 200 * 0.012 = $2,400,000. int6 cost: $0.0043/token -> monthly = $860,000. Hybrid (70% int6 / 30% fp16) = 0.7*$860k + 0.3*$2.4M = ~$1.04M. Savings vs fp16 ~56%. (I know these are rough; we'll refine with real traffic shape.)
Nina: good to include a SLA risk note — product wants to know worst-case impact.
maria: also want a one-paragraph recommendation and a short scorecard for GTN.
Sam: recommendation (short): default to int6 for latency-sensitive, short-turn traffic; route long/retrieval/summarizer to fp16. Canary 5% for 48h, evaluate slice metrics hourly; auto-fallback if EM_delta >= 0.02 over 30m. If canary passes, ramp to 25% then 50% over a week with monitoring.
Sam: I'll post a compact scorecard in this thread in ~30m with numbers, and attach the config snippet we tested.
Arjun: can you paste the routing snippet now so infra can review?
Sam: small snippet we used: 
```
route_rules:
  - match: product_tag == "summarizer" or seq_len > 1024 or has_retrieval == true
    send_to: fleet_fp16_ceruleanx_v1
  - match: default
    send_to: fleet_int6_ceruleanx_v1
fallback:
  quality_monitor:
    metric: exact_match
    threshold: 0.02
    window: 30m
    action: route_to_fp16
```
Nina: looks reasonable. Ops — watch for config rollout window.
ops-bot: Canary deployed. Monitoring dashboards: https://metrics.internal/d/ceruleanx/canary
maria: thanks — product will review and decide whether to sign off on hybrid. If they ask for a smaller perf drop margin (1%), we'll hold back.
Sam: noted. Will follow up with the scorecard and a short README for the routing flags. :thumbsup:
Nina: thanks Sam.
Arjun: thumbs up from me too.
cheng: will keep an eye on memory/kv during canary and post any anomalies here.
ops-bot: Closing note: canary job will post summary at completion.
Sam: ack, will collect eval snapshots and share.
